subject: Q1 Marketing Launch – FieldSense 200 Series

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Okay, I want to use this time to align on the launch plan for the FieldSense 200 before we commit to any external spend. We have a window in early April that I think is the right moment, and I want to make sure Sales is ready to absorb the inbound before we open the tap.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Early April works for us. Jamal and I have been warming up the pipeline for about six weeks now and we have eight prospects who are actively waiting to see the product page go live. The question I have is whether the product will actually be available to ship in April, because I don't want to generate demand we can't fulfill.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Same concern from my side. I've had two conversations this week where I had to be vague about availability and it's starting to feel awkward.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I've been checking with Devon on production status. The current read is that we'll have initial inventory of three hundred units by March 27th. That's enough to support a launch.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That aligns with what I heard from Devon last week. I think we're okay to plan around that date.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Three hundred units — what's the allocation split between the launch promotion and regular stock? If we're running a limited-time offer for early buyers, I want to make sure we're not accidentally over-committing.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I was thinking we hold fifty units aside for PR samples and any trade show demo needs, and the remaining two-fifty go into sellable inventory. We're not planning a deep discount launch — the positioning is premium, so we're not expecting a flood of impulse orders.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: What is the launch price? I still don't have a confirmed number to give prospects.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: We've been working off an assumption of eight hundred and forty dollars per unit for single quantities, with a volume break at twenty-five units dropping it to seven-ninety. Has that been finalized?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Renata and I reviewed it last week. The list price is confirmed at eight hundred and forty. The volume break at twenty-five units is approved at eight hundred even, not seven-ninety. I should have circulated that — my fault for the gap.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Good to know. Eight hundred at twenty-five units is actually a stronger story than seven-ninety because it's a rounder number.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Okay, so on the marketing side, here's what I have planned. We're doing a product launch email to the existing contact list — about four thousand addresses — on April 7th. Paid search goes live the same day. I have a contributed article placed in Industrial Sensor Quarterly that publishes April 9th. And I'm targeting a press release through Cision on April 7th as well.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Can we get the product page live a few days before the email goes out? I want to be able to send prospects a link before the public launch so they feel like they're getting early access.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I can make the page live on April 4th with a soft launch — no promotion, just accessible. That gives you a three-day window to share it selectively.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That works. Jamal, can you put together a short list of the top fifteen prospects who should get that early link?

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll have it to you and Nadia by end of this week.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I also want to talk about the messaging. The core claim I've been developing is around the FieldSense 200's accuracy in high-vibration environments. Marcus gave me some test data showing plus-or-minus 0.3 percent accuracy under conditions that would knock most competitors to plus-or-minus 2 percent. That's a real differentiator.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That's the number customers ask about first. I've heard it come up in almost every discovery call.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Make sure Callum has signed off on the accuracy claim before it goes in any external material. I don't want a claim that's going to cause us trouble if a customer tests it in a slightly different setup.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Already on my list. I have a meeting with Callum on Thursday to go through the claims language.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: One thing I've been hearing from prospects is that they want to know about integration with existing PLCs. A few of them are running older Siemens setups. Do we have documentation on that?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I don't have that in the current launch materials. Is that a firmware or hardware question?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Probably both. I'll flag it to Marcus and Sofia and see what they can give us. Even a one-page compatibility note would help.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Let's make sure that's ready before the launch email goes out. It doesn't have to be elaborate, but it needs to exist.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Agreed. I'll track it as a dependency. If it's not ready by April 4th, we may need to adjust the messaging to avoid raising the question we can't answer.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: I think we're in good shape overall. My main ask is that once the page is live on April 4th, someone is monitoring inbound form submissions in real time so we're not leaving leads sitting for days.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I'll set up a Slack notification for every form submission. Jamal, you and I should agree on a response SLA before launch.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Two business hours for the first response. I can commit to that.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Good. Let's lock this plan in. Nadia owns the launch execution. Elena and Jamal own sales readiness. I want a brief check-in the week of March 30th to confirm inventory and materials are both on track.

decisions: FieldSense 200 launch is targeted for April 7, 2026.
List price confirmed at $840 per unit; volume break at 25 units is $800, not $790.
Product page goes live April 4th as a soft launch for selective prospect sharing.
All external accuracy claims must be reviewed by Callum before publication.

action_items.task: Compile a list of the top fifteen prospects to receive the early-access product page link by end of this week.
Coordinate with Marcus and Sofia to produce a PLC compatibility note for the FieldSense 200 before April 4th.
Get legal sign-off from Callum on the accuracy claims language before finalizing launch materials.
Set up real-time Slack notifications for inbound form submissions on the product page.
